prize_parts.citation: For the prediction of flat electronic bands at magic twist angles in twisted bilayer graphene and the experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states at those angles, opening the field of moire quantum materials.

statement.case_for: I keep magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene as my single preferred prize and my position is unchanged from round 1, though the discussion has sharpened why. A quantitative prediction (the Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model, with flat bands at a definite angle) was tested by experiment (correlated insulators and superconducting domes at that angle in Jarillo-Herrero's group), and the result was then reproduced by many independent groups and carried to other moire platforms. For someone who works on statistical models of complex systems, the important point is that one geometric parameter tunes the ratio of kinetic to interaction energy in a clean, controllable two-dimensional system. That makes strongly interacting many-body physics experimentally accessible in a new way, which is a discovery about nature and not an improvement in measurement. The discussion has shown that the real disagreement is about maturity and about how to weigh the pairing mechanism, not about scientific quality, and I do not think the open mechanism should decide the case. The citation is written around what is established, the predicted flat bands and the observed states, and says nothing about the origin of the superconductivity. A three-name credit follows the prediction and demonstration split without strain.
statement.case_against: The strongest objection is the one raised by Kroll, Lindroth, Pearce and Danielsson: eight years after the key experiments the pairing mechanism, the phase diagram and the role of twist-angle disorder and strain are still debated, and a prize made later would rest on firmer ground. I take that seriously as a judgement of timing, although I would not call it a flaw in the discovery. The credit is also incomplete by construction. Lopes dos Santos, Peres and Castro Neto have an earlier moire band-structure result, and Cao, Dean, Young, Yacoby and others made essential experimental contributions that a three-name limit cannot recognise. I regard the omission of the experimental co-workers as the least comfortable part of the configuration, because a Nobel prize in experimental physics that credits only the group leader will be questioned. I accept that this is a real cost and not merely a technicality.

responses.point: Argues that a prize should rest on settled physics, that B009 should be left to mature, and that lattice clocks have two decades of independent confirmation without a comparable interpretive question.
responses.response: I accept that B049 is more mature, and I list it as my first alternative for that reason. But I do not accept that the unsettled pairing mechanism makes the physics unsettled. What is settled are the facts the citation asserts: flat bands at the predicted angle, insulating states at integer fillings and superconducting domes, all seen by several groups with different techniques. Many prizewinning discoveries in condensed matter were awarded while the mechanism was open. I also do not think the standard is applied evenly. The lattice-clock case is mature because its physics is a well-understood error budget, but that is also why it is a refinement of precision measurement, with the 2005 and 2012 prizes as close precedents, while B009 opens a new class of quantum matter. Your own caveat that the committee must verify the 10^-18 numbers, and that the Katori-Ye pair is defensible only if the omission of Lemonde and Ludlow is stated openly, shows that the clock credit is not entirely free of dispute either.

responses.point: Says the redefinition of the second should not be awaited, since the achievement is complete and waiting would reward administrative timing, and says the PTB, NIST and SYRTE confirmations support maturity.
responses.response: Your reply to my round-1 comment was fair, and I do not use the redefinition of the second as an argument against B049; I would not hold the clocks to a standard that depends on a metrological decision. The same principle cuts the other way for B009: if timing of a downstream decision should not delay recognition of a finished achievement, an unsettled pairing mechanism should not delay recognition of a finding that is already established and replicated. I therefore ask that the committee apply one maturity standard to both candidates, namely whether the central observation is robust and independently reproduced. Your atomic-structure argument that the magic-wavelength condition and the blackbody and Stark shift budgets make the 10^-18 claims credible is the kind of specialist judgement I cannot make, and it is why I regard B049 as a legitimate lead and not a weak one.

responses.point: Moved from B026 to B049 because of the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang gap, considers B009 very strong but one that gains from waiting, and asks that the committee check the specific stability and uncertainty figures for the clocks.
responses.response: I agree with you on B026: the HgTe prediction by Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang triggered the experiment, Zhang cannot be recognised, and the three-dimensional work is a separate chapter, so a Kane-Mele-Molenkamp trio leaves a visible gap. That is why B026 is only my second alternative. I disagree that B009 gains from waiting. The 2018 observations have been reproduced and extended across several moire systems, and the main way waiting would improve the prize is by resolving the mechanism, which a Nobel discovery does not require. I also share your request to verify numbers: for B049 the committee should check the published systematic uncertainty and instability figures before relying on general knowledge, and for B009 it should check that the flat-band condition and the observed states are stated precisely in the citation.

responses.point: Names maturity as the main reason a committee might wait on B009, and says the credit question should be decided by the discovery narrative while keeping the citation off the superconducting mechanism.
responses.response: We agree on the three names and on the wording. On maturity I would add one proposal for the committee: if it chooses to wait, it should say that the reason is the interpretive state of the field and not a doubt about the discovery. I would not wait, because the facts the citation states are not in dispute, but I accept that a different committee could reasonably weigh the pairing question more heavily than I do. On attribution, I think the order matters: the Bistritzer-MacDonald angle is the decisive prediction because it gave the quantitative magic-angle condition that guided the experiment, and the citation should name flat bands at specific angles to keep that credit explicit and to treat the earlier moire work honestly as precursor work.

responses.point: Argues that the credit for B009 should follow the discovery narrative, flat-band prediction then correlated phases, and that Bistritzer-MacDonald is the decisive prediction because it gave the quantitative magic-angle condition.
responses.response: I agree, and I add a caution to my own round-1 wording. Earlier continuum work identified a strongly reduced Fermi velocity at small twist angles, so the distinction between that result and the quantitative flat-band condition at a magic angle needs to be stated carefully if the committee is challenged on priority. I would also rather say clearly in the committee's note, not in the citation, that the earlier work of Lopes dos Santos, Peres and Castro Neto is recognised as precursor work. On the experimental side I still see the Jarillo-Herrero group's observation of both insulating and superconducting states at the predicted angle as the decisive demonstration, while accepting that the parallel hBN-encapsulation work and the later Dean, Young and Yacoby experiments are what established the generality of the effect.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will accept that robust, reproduced observations are sufficient for B009 while the pairing mechanism and phase diagram remain open, or will hold the prize until the field is better understood.

How to handle experimental credit beyond Jarillo-Herrero (Cao, Dean, Young, Yacoby) and the earlier moire continuum theory (Lopes dos Santos, Peres, Castro Neto) within a three-person limit, and whether the citation wording is enough to treat that fairly.

Whether B049 is distinct enough from the 2005 and 2012 precision-measurement prizes, and whether the specific stability and accuracy figures for the clocks have been checked against the published record.

I rely on general knowledge of these fields and I am a theorist of complex systems, not of moire materials or clocks, so my judgement of the experimental details of B009 and the atomic physics of B049 depends on what colleagues can confirm.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict is apparent from my documented record: none of my co-authors, supervisors or institutions (Gothenburg, Max Planck institutes, Oxford, Freiburg) is among the credited names of B009, B049 or B026. My opening support for B011 is dropped from my preferred configuration after the discussion, and I disclose only that active matter and statistical physics are close to my own field, which is why I regard my earlier view of that candidate as potentially biased. I do not claim any undocumented connection to the candidates.
